mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (or equivalent) of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Taiwan by a local notary public; then authentication by the Taiwan High Court; then verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); then verification by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); final acceptance by the Chinese government. This is a consular legalization process specific to cross-strait documents, not a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent) of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Taiwan; authentication by Taiwan High Court; SEF verification; ARATS verification; acceptance by Chinese authorities. Consular legalization via cross-strait mechanism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the WFOE formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Taiwan; authentication by Taiwan High Court; SEF verification; ARATS verification; acceptance by Chinese authorities. Consular legalization via cross-strait mechanism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Taiwan; authentication by Taiwan High Court; SEF verification; ARATS verification; acceptance by Chinese authorities. Consular legalization via cross-strait mechanism.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior management against the following lists: (1) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the People's Bank of China (PBOC) guidelines; (2) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (4) Chinese domestic sanctions lists issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Public Security; (5) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any match, including source of funds verification, adverse media screening, and enhanced transaction monitoring. For this medium-risk industry (battery-grade lithium carbonate trading), additional scrutiny is applied to cross-border wire transfers and trade finance instruments. All screening must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration System (via local SAMR bureau)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters, following the four-tier structure: administrative division + trade name + industry description + legal form (e.g., 'Shanghai [Trade Name] Lithium Carbonate Trading Co., Ltd.'). For foreign investors, the trade name may be a phonetic transliteration of the parent company's name, but must be approved by SAMR. English names are not registered but may be used for banking and trade purposes; they must be a direct translation of the Chinese name. No characters or symbols other than Chinese characters are permitted in the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the local SAMR within 15 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name complies with the naming rules, along with supporting documents. If the local SAMR upholds the rejection, the applicant may escalate to the provincial SAMR within 30 days. For final recourse, an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the People's Court within 6 months. The entire appeal process typically takes 30-60 days. It is advisable to submit a revised name application simultaneously to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not permissible for WFOE registration in China. The SAMR requires a physical, rentable office address that is verifiable and must be used for actual business operations. Tax authorities and banks also require a physical presence for VAT registration and bank account opening. For the lithium carbonate trading industry, a physical office is mandatory to demonstrate commercial substance and to satisfy the 'place of effective management' test under Chinese tax law. A virtual office would likely be rejected by the SAMR, tax bureau, and banks, and could trigger penalties for false registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered office is actually occupied and has a visible company sign; (2) Ensure that the office is not a residential address unless specifically permitted by local regulations; (3) Maintain lease agreements, utility bills, and property tax receipts; (4) Have a designated person present during business hours; (5) Ensure that the office is used for actual business activities, not just as a mail drop. Risk quantification: For a WFOE in the trading sector, the likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the local SAMR or tax bureau is moderate (30-40% within the first year). Inspections are more likely if the company applies for export tax rebates or engages in high-value cross-border transactions. The risk increases if the registered address is a shared office or a low-cost business center.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended, Articles 128, 129, 131, 154, 161, 172, 192 and 216, read together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 10-14 and 22, and the Regulations for Approval of Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal; and the Investment Commission, MOEA, for foreign-investor pre-approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Incorporation Registration (electronic) together with the executed Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited company; the share capital must be reasonably sufficient for the stated business scope. Before incorporation, the foreign founder must deposit the subscribed paid-up capital into a temporary escrow bank account opened in Taiwan under the proposed company name. The escrow bank must issue a capital balance certificate, and the capital remains blocked or escrowed until the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Thereafter the escrow account is released to the company's authorized officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED

At a meeting of the Board of Directors duly convened and held on [Date] at [Time] at [Provisional Registered Office Address], the following Directors were present in person: [Director A], [Director B] and [Director C]. [Supervisor D] attended as a statutory observer. The Chair [Director A] confirmed that the meeting had been lawfully called and that a quorum existed in accordance with Article 172 of the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation. The agenda had been circulated in advance. The Chair then proposed, and the Board unanimously resolved, as follows:

1. SUBSCRIPTION, ALLOTMENT AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The Board ratified the subscription and allotment of [100,000] ordinary shares, each of par value New Taiwan Dollars [10], issued at par to the sole shareholder [Parent Company], for aggregate paid-up share capital of New Taiwan Dollars [1,000,000]. The Board acknowledged receipt of the bank capital balance certificate issued by [Bank], Account Number [Number], evidencing that the full subscription price has been paid into the temporary escrow account. The Board declared the said capital to be fully subscribed and fully paid, approved the share register and the certificate of paid-in capital, and authorized the Chairman and Corporate Secretary to certify the same in the registration documents. Upon incorporation, the escrow account shall be converted into the Company's operating account and funds shall be applied only to lawful corporate purposes.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board formally adopted the registered office and legal seat of the Company as [Registered Office Address, Floor, District, City, Postal Code], Taiwan. The Board directed the Corporate Secretary to execute the office lease, affix the registered address to all statutory books and filings, and apply for the corporate seal bearing the exact registered company name.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorized the opening and maintenance of corporate bank accounts with [Bank] and any other domestic or foreign banks as the officers may determine. All accounts shall operate under dual-signatory authority, requiring the Chairman and the Finance Director, or in their absence the General Manager as alternate, to execute instructions. The bank account signatory specimen cards and the corporate seal specimen shall be lodged with the banks together with a certified copy of this resolution.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board unanimously appointed [Name] as Chairman and Representative Director, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Finance Director, [Name] as Corporate Secretary, and [Name] as Supervisor. Each appointee formally accepted office. The Chairman and the Supervisor are jointly authorized to execute all instruments and to represent the Company before the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, customs, labor authorities, and banks.

5. GENERAL AND FINAL AUTHORIZATION. The Board approved and authorized all officers to prepare, execute, notarize, file, and follow-up all incorporation applications, Articles of Incorporation, foreign investment permits, tax registrations, trade registrations, and any ancillary filing required to commence business. Resolved unanimously and certified as a true and complete record. [Signature of Corporate Secretary] [Name], Corporate Secretary [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan) and MOEA Name Reservation Online System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal foreign-investment application and company name reservation through the MOEA Investment Commission e-service portal. The submission must include the investor's legalized company registration, proof of ultimate beneficial ownership, proposed English and Chinese company names, exact business scope limited to wholesale of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder, registered capital amount, local office plan, and intended bank and customs arrangements. The investment project must be classified as a wholesale trade and not as a low-productivity manufacturing project. MOEA will verify compliance with negative lists under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. The application must be digitally signed by a Taiwan agent or the responsible person using a MOEACA-issued digital certificate. If the name contains words suggesting government affiliation or is identical to an existing registered name, a substitute name must be submitted within the same application.
required_dossiers: Legalized and consular-certified certificate of incorporation of ultimate parent company
Current company name reservation application form
Passport/ARC of Taiwan responsible person or agent
Business plan with proposed ISIC 4662 business scope
Power of attorney for local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or provisional rejection, the applicant may submit a supplementary response and revised investment plan within 14 calendar days through the portal. If the final decision denies the investment because of negative-list or public-interest grounds, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Executive Yuan Administrative Appeals Commission within 30 days of service, attaching the original denial notice and a legal brief on why the proposed wholesale activity is not restricted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles, Capital Escrow, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Association-affiliated civil notary and a licensed commercial bank in Taiwan as escrow agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After foreign investment approval, convene the promoters' meeting and execute the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese, stating the company name, business scope, capital, registered office, director and supervisor election rules, and name of legal representative. Each promoter or authorized representative must sign or affix the company seal. Have the signatures notarized by a Taiwan notary public to attest identity and legal capacity. Open a temporary escrow account with a licensed Taiwanese bank in the name of the proposed company and deposit the full paid-up capital. Obtain an original bank capital balance certificate showing the account name, account number, deposit date, and balance. The certificate must correspond exactly with the share subscription schedule; discrepancies will prevent registration. Deliver notarized documents and escrow certificate to legal counsel for the commercial registry filing. This capital block remains in force until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank account application forms and account-holder documents
Proposed election/consent forms of directors and supervisor
Notarized power of attorney if signed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses attestation due to identity or authority defects, cure by obtaining a clean certified copy of the parent company resolution and a revised power of attorney, then re-notarize. If the bank refuses to open the escrow account because of beneficial-ownership concerns, provide an updated source-of-funds declaration and ask for re-screening; if still refused, choose another licensed Taiwanese bank within seven days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing with MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) via the Company and Commercial Registration Information System (CCRIS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Company Incorporation Registration and supporting dossiers electronically through CCRIS or at the MOEA commercial registration service window. Complete all mandatory fields, including the approved name, business scope code 4662, registered office address, paid-up capital as shown on the bank certificate, number of shares, directors' and supervisor's particulars, and corporate seal specimen. Attach the original or digitally authenticated Articles of Incorporation, the escrow bank capital balance certificate, the investment commission approval, and written consents of directors and supervisor. The system will calculate the registration fee; pay it online within the session. Once the registry has verified that all conditions under Articles 128, 129, 131 and 154 of the Company Act are satisfied, it will issue an electronic Certificate of Incorporation and a unified company registration number. The registration must precisely match the foreign investment approval to avoid amendment filings.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease agreement or consent from owner
Residence/ID or ARC copies of directors, supervisor, and representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA suspends or queries the filing, the applicant will receive an online deficiency notice; the company must respond and submit corrected documents within 30 days. Correct missing signatures or inconsistency between capital certificate and share schedule, pay any supplemental fee, and resubmit. If the registry refuses registration, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with MOEA within 30 days after receipt of the refusal, and ultimately appeal to the Administrative Court within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Trade, and Labor/Health Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau local office, Bureau of Foreign Trade (MOEA), Bureau of Labor Insurance, and National Health Insurance Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after incorporation, apply to the local National Taxation Bureau for a uniform invoice number and tax registration certificate. Register the company's business scope with the Bureau of Foreign Trade to obtain an import/export registration and the associated electronic customs code, because the company will procure lithium carbonate powder cross-border and require import declaration capability. File a labor insurance unit with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and a National Health Insurance unit with the NHI administration, and enroll all employees. Keep tax classification, invoice format, and accounting records ready. The tax authority will verify the registered office and may inspect the standard-issue uniform invoice system. The import/export registration is not a sector-specific operating license but is a conditional statutory registration for customs clearance under the Foreign Trade Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and company registration data
Tax registration application form and particulars of directors
Business scope including 4662 wholesale trade and international trade
Lease agreement and stamp-duty payment receipt
Labor and NHI insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries the registered address, provide the lease contract, utility bill, and owner consent. If BOFT suspends the import/export registration pending tax verification, submit the tax certificate issued under the Foreign Trade Act and the certificate of incorporation; if denial continues, appeal to MOEA within 30 days. Labor insurance deficiencies are cured by filing a revised employee roster within seven days; no penalty applies if timely corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Books, Bank Account Release, and Occupational/Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs (for statutory books), local Fire Department, municipal labor administration, and the chosen commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, prepare the shareholders' register, share certificate ledger, minutes book, and company seal register. Hold the organizational meeting or first board meeting if not already held, passing the banking authorization and confirming the release of the escrow account. Submit a certified copy of the board resolution to the bank and convert the escrow account into the operating account. If the company will occupy commercial office space, file with the local fire department any fire-safety declaration needed for the premises, and with the municipal labor department the workplace safety notification and general safety plan. Since the company will not operate a factory or warehouse, no industrial civil-defense fire permit is required at this stage. Maintain an inventory of storage quantities if de minimis samples of lithium carbonate are held; any warehouse use will require a new permit assessment.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board or organizational meeting
Share register and share certificate specimens
Escrow release instruction and bank signatory forms
Office lease and fire-safety self-inspection checklist if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a different board authorization form, pass a supplemental board resolution and provide a certified minute. If the fire department flags the office occupancy classification, undertake any minor corrective works and submit a revised self-inspection form. If workplace safety notification is queried, retain a certified safety consultant to prepare the required general duty assessment and refile within fourteen days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for industrial manufacturing licensing; the relevant trade-control authority is the Bureau of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), which administers the import/export registration for cross-border procurement of lithium carbonate powder.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or factory permit is required for an ISIC 4662 wholesale trader. The company relies on the MOEA Certificate of Incorporation and the BOFT Import/Export Registration. Under the Toxic Chemical Substances Control Act, no separate operational permit is triggered by ordinary wholesale trading, and battery-grade lithium carbonate commodity distribution does not require a manufacturing license at the formation stage.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No Environmental Impact Assessment Report or Environmental Registration is required because the company will only conduct wholesale procurement and distribution; the activity does not constitute an industrial installation, waste treatment site, or land-development project listed in the EPA's EIA schedule. If future physical storage or processing is added, the operation would be re-classified and a registration or impact assessment could be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for the trading operation because there will be no process wastewater, VOC emission points, or hazardous waste generation. If future repackaging or bulk storage is introduced, the operator must comply with Taiwan Effluent Standards, that is, pH 6-9, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 100 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L unless a more stringent sector-specific standard applies; the Air Pollution Control Act emission standards for VOC fugitive sources using recovery equipment with no less than 90 percent capture; and the Waste Disposal Act requirement that all empty bags or containers contaminated with lithium carbonate powder be tested for corrosivity and leachability, with manifest and transporter permits required if classified as hazardous industrial waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No Civil Defense fire permit is required for office-only wholesale operations. Before occupying the registered office, obtain a fire safety compliance inspection or certificate from the local fire department if the floor area or occupancy classification so requires. File a workplace safety notification with the municipal labor inspection office and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by maintaining emergency evacuation plans, first aid measures, and safety data sheets for any small sample quantities of lithium carbonate. If the company later establishes a warehouse for battery materials, a separate Fire Safety Management Plan, hazardous goods storage approval, and Civil Defense-type fire permit must be obtained before operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; local National Taxation Bureau with jurisdiction over the registered place of business or fiscal agent; online electronic portal is the MOF Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform and the National Taxation Administration tax registration portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Prior to commencing Taiwan business activity, complete any applicable foreign investment approval with the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and incorporate the Taiwan entity under the Company Act. Step 2: Register the profit-seeking enterprise and business taxpayer under Article 28 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act with the local National Taxation Bureau covering the registered office or place of business in Taiwan. Step 3: For a foreign non-resident entity without a fixed place of business, appoint a Taiwan-resident fiscal representative or tax agent and register with the National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the representative or agent location. Step 4: File the standard tax registration application supported by the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, Taiwan address or agency appointment, and identification of the Taiwan responsible person, and obtain a Unified Business Number (UBIN) from the Ministry of Finance. Step 5: After the UBIN is issued, register as an E-Invoice issuer and connect to the MOF Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform through the E-Invoice Turnkey service or a certified E-Invoice service provider. Step 6: Complete profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration so that business tax, income tax, and the electronic invoice reporting obligations operate under the same UBIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification election and no standalone entity classification election is available for a limited company. The WFOE entity style is classified as a resident profit-seeking enterprise and taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act. There is no hybrid-mismatch election; any hybrid mismatch adjustment would be applied under the anti-avoidance provisions of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (VAT) under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act (Taiwan Business Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General taxable businesses have no turnover-based exemption threshold and must register before starting Taiwan business activity. A special TWD 480,000 annual Taiwan-source turnover threshold applies only to foreign electronic-service suppliers; once exceeded, the foreign seller must register for Taiwan business tax through the fiscal representative regime. Small-scale domestic businesses with average monthly sales below TWD 80,000 may qualify for simplified taxation, but this simplified status does not apply to a regular limited company carrying out battery-metal arbitrage.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan does not use a real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping model. Sellers of taxable goods or services must issue uniform invoices under Article 32 of the Business Tax Act. When E-Invoices are used, the seller must transmit invoice data to the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform within 48 hours through the E-Invoice Turnkey service or a certified E-Invoice API service provider. The platform controls invoice numbering, random-check code generation, and data validation; the National Taxation Administration matches seller and buyer data to detect under-reporting, late filing, and fraudulent invoices. Any failure to issue, transmit, or correctly report E-Invoice data is subject to the administrative penalties prescribed in the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 8 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, sales of goods that are actually exported from Taiwan and customs-cleared are zero-rated. Qualifying services rendered in Taiwan that are used outside Taiwan, or services connected with exported goods, are zero-rated only if supported by a written contract and foreign-exchange receipt evidencing that the consideration is paid by a foreign buyer. Mere procurement or arbitrage does not qualify unless physical export from Taiwan is completed and the same registered taxpayer appears as the exporter on the Commercial Invoice, the Customs Export Declaration, and the beneficiary of the foreign-exchange receipt. Creditable input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports may be offset or refunded after the supporting document package is reviewed. Importation of battery-grade lithium carbonate into Taiwan is not zero-rated; it is subject to 5% import business tax and customs duties, with input VAT recovery available to registered taxpayers under normal VAT principles.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) approved by Taiwan Customs through the Ministry of Finance Customs Administration Single Window
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving actual cross-border movement of the lithium carbonate powder
Commercial Invoice and Packing List describing the goods, quantity, unit value, and export destination

Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate or bank inward-remittance settlement record, equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), showing the export proceeds were collected from the overseas buyer
Export sales contract, purchase order, or pro forma invoice linking the shipment and the foreign-exchange receipt to the zero-rated sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Administration may audit export zero-rating claims retrospectively, ordinarily for five years, but longer where fraud or material misreporting is suspected. If the required Customs Export Declaration, transport document, Commercial Invoice, and foreign-exchange receipt are not complete or do not tie to the same counterparty, the zero-rated treatment is clawed back and output VAT is reassessed at the standard 5% rate with late interest under the Tax Collection Act. Administrative penalties under the Business Tax Act may be imposed up to five times the underpaid tax, and materially false export documentation, forged customs filings, or fraudulent refund claims may lead to criminal liability under the tax evasion provisions of the Tax Collection Act and the penalty provisions of the Customs Act. Failure to repatriate and settle export foreign exchange within 180 days without the approval of Taiwan's central bank also exposes the entity to fines and enforcement measures under the Management of Foreign Exchange Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); the Taiwan parent's outbound investment approval rests with the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission, but the WFOE's onshore FX regime is exclusively governed by PBOC and SAFE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is not freely convertible on the capital account. Current account trade items, such as import settlement for battery-grade lithium carbonate, commissions, freight, and related trade expenses, are substantially convertible after verification of genuine underlying transactional documents through a licensed PRC bank. Capital account inflows, including the WFOE's paid-in share capital, require SAFE-registered FDI project status, a bank-recorded foreign investment code, and strict compliance with the actual-use principle. Inbound equity funds may only enter through a designated FDI foreign exchange capital account and must be settled into RMB for verified business purposes; they cannot be used for equity investment, intercompany lending, securities purchases, or FX speculation. Profit remittance to the Taiwan parent is permitted after the annual statutory audit, final tax clearance, board resolution, audited financial statements, and SAFE/CRS-related reporting, but the bank must confirm no unpaid taxes, no unresolved SAFE penalty, and a clean trade verification classification. Retained earnings may be remitted in the original FDI currency through the current account channel, subject to genuineness checks and documentary support.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has no fixed statutory percentage of export proceeds that must be converted into RMB; the original mandatory surrender regime was replaced by repatriation and retention controls. All goods-trade export revenues must be repatriated into China through an eligible bank account within the normal trade settlement cycle, and SAFE's trade monitoring system generates exception reports for any receivable outstanding beyond 180 days from the customs export declaration date unless an offshore retention has been separately approved. The bank verifies the receipt against the customs declaration, contract, and commercial invoice through the SAFE-linked goods-trade monitoring system. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain export receipts in USD or another foreign currency or voluntarily sell them to the settlement bank. Non-repatriation, prolonged outstanding balances, or mismatches between goods flow and funds flow can result in a downgrade of the enterprise verification classification and tighter documentary scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable for primary onboarding. Offshore digital EMIs licensed in Hong Kong, Singapore, the UK, or elsewhere are not licensed by PBOC and cannot provide SAFE-compliant RMB settlement accounts to a PRC-incorporated WFOE. They cannot perform FDI capital registration, cannot receive funds into a statutory capital account with the required foreign exchange purpose code, and cannot verify trade-in-goods documentation under SAFE rules. At most, an offshore EMI could support ancillary multi-currency receivables for the Taiwan parent outside mainland China, but such a rail cannot be used to bypass the WFOE's onshore banking obligations. Legal rating: restricted/unavailable for the WFOE treasury mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person branch appearance is mandatory for the WFOE's legal representative or sole executive director, and usually the financial controller, when opening the basic settlement account. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognized by PBOC account-opening rules for the initial KYC interview, although cross-strait notarized powers of attorney may be accepted for subsequent signatory changes. The bank will require the original business license, company chops, board resolution, articles of association, UBO declaration, source-of-funds narrative, and a face-to-face interview covering the business plan, intended cross-border flows, and the lithium carbonate procurement model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from nominee shareholders or Taiwan shelf holding companies with limited economic substance and no clear source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration and full ownership chain; Taiwan MOEA Investment Commission outbound investment approval; three years of audited financial statements for the investor; bank reference letter from the Taiwan home bank; notarized board resolution approving the capital contribution; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files, including tax returns, bank statements, and purchase/sale documents for the original capital; physical office and employee evidence for the investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag where lithium carbonate invoice prices deviate materially from independent market benchmarks or move through multiple intermediary shell traders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding purchase and sale contracts specifying battery-grade lithium carbonate quality, typically Li2CO3 purity above 99.5%; SMM, Fastmarkets, ICIS, or Platts benchmark price screens; independent SGS, Intertek, or similar quality and weight certificates; full transport documentation including bills of lading, customs declarations, warehouse receipts, and freight invoices; reconciliation between goods quantities, pricing formula, payment milestones, and delivery dates; copies of end-user offtake agreements or OEM orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-trip risk where the Taiwan investor injects registered capital and the WFOE immediately disburses most of the funds to an overseas supplier on the same value date, creating an FX arbitrage or disguised financing pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 24-month liquidity forecast and capital deployment schedule; supplier KYC and due-diligence file; procurement contract and underlying commercial rationale; customer purchase orders or battery manufacturer offtakes; payment milestone calendar matching supply-chain lead times; board-approved treasury policy; certificate from a PRC CPA verifying the capital use, if required, and confirmation that the funds support genuine operating liquidity rather than speculative settlement movements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted-destination exposure in the battery metals supply chain, including transshipment through high-risk free-trade zones or involvement of vessels and counterparties linked to sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, EU, UN, and Chinese sanctioned-party screening results for all payees, intermediaries, ships, and vessel IMO numbers; country-of-origin certificates and bill-of-lading routing evidence; customs import/export declarations; supplier compliance attestation; end-user and end-use attestation letters; cargo insurance and maritime documentation; contractual clauses incorporating international sanctions and anti-money-laundering requirements; complete trade-based money-laundering red-flag checklist signed by the compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must first complete any applicable Taiwan MOEA Investment Commission outbound filing, and the WFOE must complete SAFE FDI registration through a licensed PRC bank to obtain the FDI enterprise code. The inbound remittance should be sent as a SWIFT MT103 with the payment purpose identified as FDI capital injection, referencing the WFOE's registration code and unique identifier. Funds must be credited only to the registered FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and must not be commingled with trade receipts or operating collections. Each conversion from foreign exchange into RMB requires a bank-verified actual-use capital settlement declaration, and the resulting RMB must be applied within the WFOE's licensed business scope. A CPA capital verification report should be prepared for statutory filing and annual audit purposes, and any subsequent movement to operational accounts must be routed through the bank's SAFE-integrated settlement system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to overseas lithium carbonate suppliers should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlement or pre-payment, through commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) for large documentary purchases, and through documentary collections (DP/DA) for established suppliers. The instructing bank must verify the import contract, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration, and match the payment against the applicable SAFE goods-trade foreign-exchange transaction code and the enterprise verification classification. If the supplier accepts RMB, the payment should be routed through CIPS or cross-border RMB settlement to minimize FX conversion and the retained earnings exposure. Where goods enter through a bonded zone or free-trade area, import duty and VAT settlement should be handled separately in compliance with tax regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with notional and maturity matched to signed lithium carbonate purchase contracts, executed through a licensed PRC bank under the SAFE real-demand principle.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where there is an unambiguous underlying foreign-currency payables or trade-financing exposure linked to the battery metals procurement cycle.
FX swaps between RMB and USD/EUR with commercial trade flows as the underlying transaction and no speculative open position.
Premium-bearing FX option strategies bought by the WFOE for downside protection; selling uncovered option structures is restricted and not permitted for ordinary treasury hedging.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for a PRC WFOE because SAFE requires a genuine deliverable or physical settlement trade posture; any synthetic NDF-only arrangement would violate the actual-transaction principle and is not bankable onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Report, and Profit Distribution or Loss Absorption Proposal (annual shareholder/contributor approval under Company Act Articles 20 and 228 for a foreign-invested limited company/WFOE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the WFOE; certified approving minutes and audited statements are available for inspection by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Commercial Administration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 June of the year following the fiscal year end (within six months after the fiscal year end for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or obtain shareholder approval can result in an administrative fine of NT$10,000-50,000 on the responsible person under the Company Act; after a 30-day remediation notice, the competent authority may order dissolution or administrative strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Registration Data Confirmation and Amendment Filing (Register of Members, Directors, and Registered Address; no-change declaration preserved in the corporate minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Commercial Administration Office / Central Company Registration Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after any registrable change occurs; if there are no annual changes, the WFOE must still complete an internal annual verification of the registered particulars by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a registrable change within the 15-day window attracts fines of NT$10,000-50,000; ongoing failure to maintain correct registry details can lead to suspension of foreign-investment approval and ultimately administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and supporting audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration (local district tax office for the WFOE's registered address)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; non-calendar-year taxpayers must file on or before the last day of the fourth month after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers a 3% surcharge on the unpaid tax for every two-month period of delay (maximum 10%), delinquency interest at the current annual tax interest rate, and an added penalty of up to three times the under-stated tax amount; repeated non-filing can trigger seizure of assets and criminal tax-liability prosecution within the ten-year collection window.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (VAT) Periodic Returns and Remittance (monthly or bimonthly filing under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration (local district VAT office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 15th day of the following month for monthly filers; by the 15th day of the month following the end of each two-month period for bimonthly small business filers; the annual VAT/income-tax reconciliation is embedded in the 31 May settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NT$1,500 plus NT$15,000 for prolonged non-filing; underpaid VAT is subject to a penalty of two times (unintentional) or five times (fraudulent) the under-paid amount; enforced collection may lead to freezing of bank accounts, lien over assets, and application to the court for compulsory strike-off of the Taiwan registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Investment Operation Survey and UBO/AML Beneficial-Ownership Confirmation (foreign investment annual survey response and update of UBO records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), and internal AML compliance records subject to examination by the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The MOEA Investment Commission annual survey for the preceding calendar year is due by 31 May of the following year; any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change must be reflected in the statutory registers within 30 days and filed/updated with MOEA within the applicable 15-day company-registration window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond to the annual foreign-investment survey may cause suspension or revocation of the foreign-investment approval; failure to maintain accurate UBO/AML records is punishable by fines of NT$500,000 to NT$10,000,000 under the Money Laundering Control Act, accompanied by an administrative order to rectify within 30 days.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan-registered WFOE limited company is mandatorily audited by an independent certified public accountant if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded at the balance-sheet date: (a) paid-in capital at least NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 950,000) under Company Act Article 20; (b) total assets at least NT$300,000,000 (approximately USD 9.5 million) or annual operating revenue at least NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3.2 million) under the business-entity accounting rules applied by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Financial Supervisory Commission; or (c) annual average full-time headcount of 100 or more employees where the company is classified as a larger business entity for audit and corporate-governance assessment. A compulsory audit also applies regardless of size to banks, insurance, securities, futures, electronic-payment, and other financial institutions supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public WFOEs below these thresholds may prepare unreviewed financial statements, but any shareholder, lender, or the Investment Commission may require a CPA audit under contractual or foreign-investment approval conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For public companies and FSC-regulated entities: Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. For ordinary non-public WFOEs: Business Entity Accounting Act, ROC GAAP (Statements of Financial Accounting Standards), or the Taiwan SME Financial Reporting Standards where eligible; statutory amounts and financial statements must be expressed in New Taiwan Dollars and, if IFRS is adopted for financing/group purposes, full IFRS with no carve-outs may be used.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose an annual standalone UBO filing for a non-public WFOE, but the company must maintain a current UBO register and incorporate the UBO confirmation into the annual foreign-investment survey and annual accounts. Any share transfer or change in direct/indirect beneficial ownership must be written into the Register of Members and the UBO register no later than 30 days after the transaction; the same change must be filed with MOEA within the 15-day company registration window if it affects directors, capital, or corporate address. The corporate secretary must verify, at least annually immediately before the shareholder approval, that the statutory registers reconcile with the latest share transfers, dividend declarations, and foreign-investment approval.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600-1,500 per year for a Taiwan registered office/registered agent with corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-9,000 for a standalone WFOE under ROC GAAP with annual revenue below USD 10 million; USD 9,000-20,000 if IFRS consolidated-group audit, intercompany transfer-pricing documentation, and tax-hearing support are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 20% preferential rate for small and micro enterprises with taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million and meeting qualifying conditions; additional 100% super-deduction on qualifying R&D expenses; 15% preferential rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); 15% preferential rate for certain encouraged industries in Western China and for enterprises in qualifying special economic zones / Pilot Free Trade Zones under specific provincial rules; 10% preferential rate for Qualifying Integrated Circuit Enterprises and certain encouraged software enterprises under the relevant circulars.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 'Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (A Class)' filed with the in-charge State Taxation Administration (STA) via the Electronic Taxpayer Portal (e-Tax @ China / 电子税务局) as part of the annual EIT settlement; supplemented by Form A105000 (Adjusted Taxable Income), Form A107012 (R&D Expense Super Deduction), Form A109000 (Cross-Border Transactions), and Form A108000 (Foreign Tax Credit).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual EIT settlement return must be filed within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (i.e. by May 31 of the following calendar year); quarterly provisional returns and prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross sales and service revenue recognized in the China-sourced profit and loss statement, including export sales routed through Taiwan. Ensure intercompany sales to the Taiwan parent or affiliates are priced at arm's length; adjust revenue if transfer pricing adjustments are made. Do not net out cross-border commissions or overseas logistics fees from revenue; any such expenses must be separately itemized. Include deemed China-sourced income from offshore procurement arbitrage if the contract, negotiation, or delivery risk is managed by the WFOE in China.

Report the cost of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder inventory and directly attributable logistics, customs, and warehousing costs. Maintain full supporting documentation for intercompany purchase prices paid to Taiwan or offshore suppliers. If the WFOE purchases from a Taiwan affiliate and resells to a China customer, the resale price method or TNMM should be applied; a gross margin lower than the functionally comparable range will trigger a transfer pricing audit. No cost deduction is available for undocumented management fees remitted to Taiwan unless the fee satisfies the Beneficial Owner and Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before adjustment (利润总额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute accounting profit before tax in accordance with PRC GAAP. Reconcile any book-tax differences including non-deductible expenses (e.g. excessive entertainment expenses, fines, and penalties) and non-taxable income. For non-resident-controlled WFOEs, this line must reflect the full accrual of sales income even if cash settlement occurs via Swift LC or wire transfer after year-end; unpaid intercompany payables to Taiwan are treated as deemed distributions or loans if left outstanding beyond the statutory period and may be recharacterized by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after tax adjustment (纳税调整后所得)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing upward adjustments, and withholding tax borne by the WFOE on behalf of the Taiwan recipient. Apply the 5-year loss carryforward deduction only for qualifying losses; losses of a WFOE that is a shell with no economic substance in China may be disallowed. Include any negative adjustment for the 100% R&D super-deduction if qualifying battery-technology R&D is performed in China. Neglect of Form A105000 reconciliation is the principal cause of EIT under-reporting penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate, computed tax, and preferential tax reduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the headline 25% statutory rate, then deduct preferential reductions: 20% small-and-micro rate, 15% HNTE rate, or 15% encouraged-industry zone rate as applicable. A WFOE merely arranging battery-metal arbitrage without manufacturing or substantive engineering in China will generally not qualify for HNTE. The effective tax rate must be reconciled with the average effective rate of the MNE group; an effective rate below the group's median without valid preferential status is a fatal transfer pricing red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and tax payable after credit (抵免税额与实际应纳所得税额)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report China tax payable offset by foreign income tax credits only for foreign-source income that is declared in China. If the Taiwan affiliate has withheld tax on royalties or interest paid by the WFOE, that Taiwan WHT may be creditable only if the income is also taxable in China and the DTA allocation rules are respected. Do not claim a foreign tax credit for Taiwan WHT if the contract lacks beneficial ownership documentation, because the DTA claim will be denied and double taxation will result.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the quarterly prepayment or annual settlement is subject to a late fee of 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax (surtax), plus a general fine of RMB 2,000–10,000 for failure to file on time; if the underpayment exceeds 10% of the tax properly payable, a fine of 50%–500% of the underpaid tax is imposed under Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law (TACL); criminal liability for fraudulent filing or false invoices applies where the underpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes tax evasion, punishable with up to 7 years' imprisonment plus criminal fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the cross-strait DTA treatment under the PRC-Taiwan Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (or the applicable arrangement / tax agreement), the Taiwan resident corporate shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Taiwan competent authority for the fiscal year in which the dividend is declared, showing beneficial ownership of the shares; (2) provide a completed 'Application for Treaty Benefit Statement' and Form CN-104 / Certificate of Residence to the China in-charge tax authority before the distribution is made; (3) substantiate that the Taiwan recipient is the beneficial owner and not a conduit, with substance evidence such as office premises, employees, bank accounts, and board minutes in Taiwan; (4) submit the withholding tax reduction application to the tax authority for approval or record-filing; and (5) obtain the tax authority's notification before remitting the dividend. Absent prior filing, the paying WFOE must withhold at the statutory 10% rate and the Taiwan shareholder may file a refund claim within the statutory limitation period, but the risk of denial is high if the offshore entity lacks economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid by a Chinese enterprise to a non-resident is 10%; under the PRC-Taiwan arrangement, treaty-relief may reduce the rate for qualifying beneficial owners, generally to 5% for interest derived by financial institutions or 10% where no specific limitation applies, and royalties typically remain subject to 10% absent a specific treaty provision; the applicant must provide TRC, beneficial ownership statement, and evidence that the Taiwan entity has both legal and economic entitlement to the income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual related-party transactions in a single year exceeding RMB 100 million for related-party tangible property transactions (goods), or RMB 40 million for related-party financial transactions (interest), or RMB 10 million for other related-party transactions (services, intangibles, royalties) trigger mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; entities with related-party controlled transactions exceeding RMB 100 million in total and with revenue above the threshold must also file Form A109000 and prepare contemporaneous documentation within the statutory period (before May 31 of the following year).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) under Article 47 of the EIT Law and the 'beneficial owner' / substance-over-form doctrine under SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9; the WFOE must have personnel, offices, decision-making functions, and inventory risk in China; a mere procurement-conduit or paper entity with no CIGA will be recharacterized, its related-party invoices disregarded, and the income reallocated to the Taiwan principal under the substance-over-form doctrine; the Economic Substance requirement is integrated with the BEPS Action Plan and the China Anti-Avoidance framework, though Taiwan's separate ESR regime is not directly applicable to a China WFOE.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Shell Company / General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a WFOE with no office, full-time employees, or independent decision-making, engaging in circular lithium-carbonate procurement between China and Taiwan solely to shift profit from China to Taiwan via inflated intercompany purchase prices or unreported commission fees, and filing zero or near-zero EIT while the Taiwan parent retains the commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 41 and Article 47 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law empower the tax authority to make transfer pricing adjustments and recharacterize the whole arrangement; Article 63 of the TACL imposes a fine of 50%–500% of the underpaid tax and late surcharge; the immediate assessment may include 100% of the adjusted tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the PRC Company Law and the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil, the sole shareholder of a one-person WFOE bears unlimited joint liability for the company's tax debts if the shareholder fails to prove the corporate assets are separate from personal assets; the legal representative ('法定代表') may be blacklisted and subject to a travel ban (exit restriction) under the 'Cooperative Punishment Memorandum for Tax-Related Offenses' if the unpaid tax exceeds the threshold; criminal liability for tax evasion carries up to 7 years' imprisonment, and where fraudulent fake invoices (虚开增值税专用发票) are used, the legal representative may be imprisoned for up to 10 years or life, with seizure of personal assets for restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Deficiency and Wrong Arm's Length Method
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare Local File / Master File / Benchmarking Study despite related-party sales exceeding RMB 100 million, or using the resale price method at a sub-functional gross margin without a comparability analysis for battery-grade lithium carbonate trading, resulting in the China WFOE reporting an effective operating margin below the interquartile range of independent commodity traders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 44 and 48 of the EIT Law and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42 / 2017 No. 6: the tax authority may use unspecified methods (e.g. hidden reserves or profit split) to adjust taxable income, apply a 5-year look-back period, impose a 5-year onward adjustment on subsequent years, and levy late interest; failure to produce documentation on demand after notice leads to a presumption of underpayment and a fine under Article 44 of TACL of up to RMB 50,000 plus a surcharge; the adjusted tax amount may be subject to a 50% penalty if deemed willful.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial director, and tax agent may be jointly and severally liable for the assessed TP adjustment if they signed inaccurate contemporaneous documentation knowing it to be false; the court may pierce the veil where personal use of company funds triggered the adjustment or where the under-capitalized WFOE is operated as an instrument of the Taiwan parent; directors may face disqualification from serving as legal representatives of any enterprise in China and a travel ban until the assessment is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and DTA/FATCA/CRS Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, paying management fees, royalties, or interest to the Taiwan shareholder without withholding the statutory 10% WHT, and failing to file the withholding return or to submit the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence, while routing funds through third-country bank accounts to disguise the outbound payment as a non-taxable loan or trade prepayment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 37 of the EIT Law requires withholding; under Article 69 of TACL the withholding agent who fails to withhold is liable for a fine equal to 50%–300% of the unwithheld tax; if the WFOE failed to remit withheld tax within the statutory time limit, a daily late surcharge of 0.05% applies; failure to report under the Cross-Border Information Reporting and CRS also triggers administrative penalties of RMB 10,000–100,000 per instance; the non-resident shareholder may additionally be assessed directly and blacklisted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instructed payment without WHT are personally accountable under Article 20 of TACL as the persons in charge of the withholding agent, with joint liability for the fine and tax; the legal representative's personal assets may be frozen, bank accounts in China may be placed under control, and an exit ban will be issued until the full tax, penalty, and surcharge are paid; criminal liability for evasion of withheld tax under Article 203 of the PRC Criminal Law exposes the director to imprisonment for up to 7 years for failing to pay the withheld tax after obtaining it, plus restitution of the misappropriated amounts.
